# Optical and Attribute Enhancement

Also called: Textured-GS, Attribute-Conditioned SH Enhancement, Defocus Blur Modeling

## Overview
Optical and Attribute Enhancement extends the standard 3D Gaussian [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) representation by allowing spatial variation of color and opacity within individual Gaussian primitives, rather than treating them as uniform ellipsoids with fixed view-dependent color. It solves the limitation of low-order [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) (SH) in capturing high-frequency details and complex surface properties by introducing per-Gaussian texture maps and static attribute-conditioned offsets. It differs from standard 3DGS by evaluating SH basis functions on surface intersection vectors ([Textured-GS](#9436-textured-gs.md)) or baking MLP-predicted offsets into parameters (Attribute-Conditioned SH), and differs from naive blurring by selectively adjusting Gaussian scales based on defocus depth [S1].

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of enhancing the visual fidelity of 3D Gaussians beyond the standard single-color, single-opacity model. All methods operate on the Gaussian primitives defined by position, rotation, scale, and base opacity. They modify the rendering or optimization pipeline to introduce higher-frequency detail or optical effects without necessarily increasing the number of primitives.

## Subtopics

### [Textured-GS](9436-textured-gs.md)
Textured-GS models spatially defined color and opacity variations across the Gaussian ellipsoidal surface using Spherical Harmonics (SH), evaluated against the surface normal rather than the viewing direction [9436-textured-gs.md]. It allows for deviations from standard ellipsoidal shapes, such as unidirectional opacity, and differs from [Gaussian Geometry Parameters Prediction](8442-gaussian-geometry-parameters-prediction.md) by using the surface intersection vector for [SH evaluation](#3848-spherical-harmonics-evaluation.md) [9436-textured-gs.md].

### [Attribute-Conditioned SH Enhancement](15410-attribute-conditioned-sh-enhancement.md)
This module recovers high-frequency visual details lost in low-order SH representations by predicting view-independent offsets via an MLP, which are statically baked into Gaussian parameters before inference [15410-attribute-conditioned-sh-enhancement.md]. It differs from dynamic neural view-dependent enhancement methods by introducing zero additional computational overhead during rendering [15410-attribute-conditioned-sh-enhancement.md].

### Defocus Blur Modeling
Models optical defocus by adjusting the scale $s$ of 3D Gaussians based on their distance from the camera's focal plane [S1]. During training, larger scale values $\hat{s}_j$ are used to rasterize blurred images, while smaller scale values $s_j$ are used during testing to render sharp details [S1]. Unlike a naive Gaussian kernel that blurs the entire image uniformly, this method selectively enlarges covariances only for Gaussians corresponding to blurred regions [S1].

## Background
The concept of modeling defocus blur using Gaussian scales originates from the observation that 3D Gaussians with greater dispersion (larger scale $s$) can represent scene points not located at the focal distance, while smaller scales model points at the focal distance [S1]. This approach was formalized in "[Deblurring 3D Gaussian Splatting](#12318-deblurring-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)" [S1], which demonstrated that larger scale values are needed to adjust 3D Gaussians to rasterize blurred training images, whereas smaller-sized Gaussians are more suitable for modeling fine details in sharp testing images [S1]. The method avoids the limitations of naive Gaussian kernels, which blur the entire image and fail to model spatially varying blurriness [S1].
